name: vault.consolidation.orphan_free
description: After a successful prune: zero ghost HNSW vectors remain (l2_index_meta rows deleted in same transaction, HNSW remove() called only after SQL commit), zero orphaned mros rows remain (deleted in same transaction as body DELETE), and survivor CDRO identity (oid_hex, canonical_hash) is unchanged. On any skip path (live_ref, tombstone_exists, governance_exempt, invalid_reason), HNSW remove() is never called (MF-3).
assertions: l2_index_meta row for pruned object deleted in the same transaction as body DELETE
mros row for pruned object deleted in the same transaction as body DELETE
HNSW remove() called for pruned vector_id and NOT called for survivor vector_id
survivor CDRO oid_hex and canonical_hash unchanged after prune of a different object
survivor mros and l2_index_meta rows intact after prune of a different object
live_ref skip: HNSW remove() is never called (MF-3); body and l2_index_meta row intact

name: vault.consolidation.scope_isolated
description: Consolidation sweep runs per-scope. A supersedes pointer that does not resolve within the caller's scope causes walkChainInScope to throw ChainScopeViolation (fail closed). The sweep catches it, records it in errors[], and continues without crashing. The object is NOT tombstoned. CDROs in other scopes are never touched by a scope-A sweep.
source: VAULT_COMPOUNDING_SUBSTRATE_SPEC.md section 6.4 Rule C, section 6.10 / F9
assertions: cross-scope supersedes pointer throws ChainScopeViolation with correct supersedes_pointer and caller_scope
in-scope chain (c->b->a all in scope-a) resolves correctly without throwing
CDROs in scope-b are untouched (oid_hex and canonical_hash unchanged) by a scope-a sweep
no tombstone written for scope-b objects during a scope-a sweep
cross-scope pointer encountered during prune-enabled sweep lands in errors[], object NOT tombstoned
walkChainInScope never resolves foreign-scope content (allowGlobal is never true on the prune path)

name: vault.consolidation.resumable
description: The consolidation sweep is resumable (cursor-based pagination via consolidation_state) and idempotent (interrupted+re-run never double-tombstones or skips objects).
assertions: sweep resumes from last_swept_object_id on restart
re-running on a fully-swept scope is a no-op (no double-tombstones)
tombstone append is idempotent per object_id
